key_insight: POD filtering helps a machine-learning surrogate distinguish turbine wakes from complex river turbulence, reducing mean squared error by three orders of magnitude versus training on unfiltered LES data.
engineering_relevance: Fast predictions of mean downstream flow could support marine hydrokinetic turbine layout optimization in natural waterways.
method: Generate instantaneous flow data using large eddy simulation (LES).
Apply proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and select modes that retain wake-relevant structures.
Train a 3D convolutional encoder–decoder to predict time-averaged velocity fields.
evidence_signal: At a real-world tidal river site under ebb conditions, the POD-filtered surrogate outperformed the unfiltered-data baseline at equivalent network size and training cost.
watch_item: Generalization to other sites, tidal conditions, and turbine layouts is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
